target_customer: Software teams that want chat-with-data agents inside customer-facing applications
problem: Letting end users ask questions of production data in plain language needs safe queries, permissions and observability. Inconvo offered an open-source platform for building such data agents.
business_model: Developer platform, open source core with a hosted product
product_category: Natural language analytics and data agents API

founders.name: Eoghan Mulcahy
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder with no background.

founders.name: Liam Mulcahy
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder with no background.

exit.reason: Attio announced the Inconvo team joined its engineering team and Inconvo says the product was sunset; the founders gave no detailed reason

technical_complexity.rationale: Natural language to SQL with permissions and safe execution was an active problem in 2023 with LLMs; building a reliable multi tenant version took real engineering but used public models.

defensibility.rationale: The core was open sourced before the sale and text-to-SQL tools were widely available, so copying it was easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it as sourced. In 2026 a CRM company, Attio, absorbed the team and technology.

market_need_then: No dated demand evidence was found. Company pages say users built data agents and the founders later concluded this technology works best integrated into tools teams already use.

branding.domain_note: Used inconvo.com per the company website.
branding.community_and_virality: Open sourced the codebase in 2026, which stays on GitHub; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found no press about the name or logo; the name hints at conversation but is little known.

outcome_analysis: Inconvo built an open-source chat-with-data platform from a two person team and no public funding was found. In mid 2026 it open sourced the code, sunset the product and the founders joined Attio's engineering team. This reads as an acquihire style landing where the product ended, in a category crowded by text-to-SQL tools and general assistants. The deal price was not disclosed.
notes: The YC directory status is Active but the company's blog and Attio's blog show the product was sunset and the team joined Attio, so exit is recorded as acquisition. The exact deal date (7 Jul 2026) and a June 19, 2026 shutdown date come from third party aggregators only, so the date is approximate. Deal terms are undisclosed. Stage labels such as acquihire and market_timing_late are my reading of the sources, not founder statements; the founders did not state a reason. A dated competitor search found only 2026 comparison pages, so the list is empty. Funding is unknown, not zero.
